newsitem.title: USA: Glaxo Wellcome sees 20 new drug launches.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome sees 20 new drug launches.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome expects by the year 2000 to launch 20 new drugs, as part of its strategy to offset declining sales of its anti-ulcer drug Zantac, deputy chairman and chief executive Sir Richard Sykes said.

"We anticipate launching 20 new products between now and teh end of the decade," Sykes told the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference here. "We have to managed the decline of Zantac by building our portfolio in other areas."
He said the six main areas where Glaxo aimed to strengthen its leadership were in herpes, asthma, viral, AIDS/HIV, migraine and epilepsy drugs.
Sykes said that while Glaxo asthma drugs already account for about 25 percent of the worldwide market, "we still see significant opportunity for growth in that area."
"We are still underrepresented in the U.S. market, which we split with Schering-Plough (Corp ). With new products, I am sure we can grow our business there."
He said new drugs to treat herpes also had the potential to capture a significant share of the market since a large portion of herpes sufferers is still treated with non- presciption drugs.
